proofs.proof_tex:
By the support-cleaning algebra lemma, \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\) has all of the asserted deterministic consequences.  Moreover,
\[
 P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}^{\mathsf c})
 =P\!\left(\frac{r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}}{\tau_{S,n}}>1\right)
 \longrightarrow0
\]
because \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\).

It remains to prove the conditional-zero bound.  All fitted objects below are recomputed from \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\); in particular \(\widehat B=\bar M_A\odot\bar M_Z\).  Both summands in \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\) lie in \(\operatorname{range}(\widehat N)=\ker(\widehat B^{\mathsf T})\): the first by definition of \(\widehat N\), and the second because every column of \(\widehat h=\widehat N\widehat c\) lies in that range.  Spectral thresholding changes only the coefficients of their linear combination.  Hence, cellwise,
\[
 \widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat k=0. \tag{1}
\]
Under three-view conditional independence, the true conditional cell law is \(d=Bw\).  Conditioning on \((Y,X)\), applying (1), and using \(g(y\mid x)w_j(y,x)=\pi_j(x)f_j(y\mid x)\) give
\[
 E_P(\widehat k\mid X=x)
 =\sum_{j=1}^{K}\pi_j(x)\int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid x)
 \{B_{\cdot j}(x)-\widehat B_{\cdot j}(x)\}^{\mathsf T}
 \widehat k(y,x)\,d\nu(y). \tag{2}
\]
Write \(\Delta_A=M_A-\bar M_A\) and \(\Delta_Z=M_Z-\bar M_Z\).  Columnwise tensor algebra yields the exact identity
\[
 B_{\cdot j}-\widehat B_{\cdot j}
 =\Delta_{A,\cdot j}\otimes M_{Z,\cdot j}
  +M_{A,\cdot j}\otimes\Delta_{Z,\cdot j}
  -\Delta_{A,\cdot j}\otimes\Delta_{Z,\cdot j}. \tag{3}
\]
The tangent-space completeness and finite-projector theorems imply
\[
 E_P(k\mid A,J,X)=0,
 \qquad E_P(k\mid Z,J,X)=0. \tag{4}
\]
Consider the term in (2)--(3) that is linear in \(\Delta_A\) and contains \(k\).  If \(M_A(x)_{aj}>0\), then (4), three-view conditional independence, and the dominated outcome law imply
\[
 \int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid x)
 \sum_zM_Z(x)_{zj}k_{az}(y,x)\,d\nu(y)=0. \tag{5}
\]
If \(M_A(x)_{aj}=0\), then on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\) also \(\bar M_A(x)_{aj}=0\), so \(\Delta_A(x)_{aj}=0\).  Thus the entire linear \(\Delta_A\)-term containing \(k\) is zero.  The symmetric use of the second equality in (4) proves the same fact for the linear \(\Delta_Z\)-term.  Notice that conditioning in (5) is used only on positive-probability cells; true-zero cells are handled algebraically.

Substitute \(\widehat k=k+(\widehat k-k)\) in the two linear terms of (3).  The preceding cancellations leave only two terms that are linear in a cleaned measurement error and linear in \(\widehat k-k\), plus the product term in \((\Delta_A,\Delta_Z)\).  Latent positivity, the cleaned half-margin conditions, boundedness of \(Y\), and \(\|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2/\varepsilon\) give a uniform \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\) bound for \(k\) and \(\widehat k\).  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz in (2), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz over \(P_X\), the fixed value of \(K\), and the cleaned \(L^2\) bounds from the support-cleaning algebra lemma therefore give
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\right].
\]
This proves the claim.

Work coordinatewise and put \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\).  The assumption \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\) is precisely \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\).  The support-cleaned conditional-zero lemma therefore applies on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\), whose probability tends to one, and gives
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\right]. \tag{6}
\]
The established score-stability lemma, applied to the same cleaned coherent law and the corrected definition of \(R_\Sigma\), gives
\[
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma. \tag{7}
\]
Combining (6) and (7),
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{(r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})R_\Sigma
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\}. \tag{8}
\]

We next evaluate the raw bridge mean.  The fitted inverse bridges are formed from \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\).  For \(j,l\in\mathcal J\), define
\[
 \delta^A_{jl}(X)=E_P\{\widehat a_j(A,X)\mid J=l,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=l\},
 \qquad
 \delta^Z_{jl}(X)=E_P\{\widehat z_j(Z,X)\mid J=l,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=l\}.
\]
By the bridge definitions and the true conditional measurement laws,
\[
 \delta^A=\bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K=\bar M_A^{-1}(M_A-\bar M_A),
 \qquad
 \delta^Z=\bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K=\bar M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\bar M_Z). \tag{9}
\]
The cleaned singular-value half-margins and the support-cleaning algebra lemma imply
\[
 \|\delta^A\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^{\mathrm c},
 \qquad
 \|\delta^Z\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^{\mathrm c}, \tag{10}
\]
and both matrices are uniformly bounded.

Conditional three-view independence separates \(Y,A,Z\) given \((J,X)\), and the definition of \(m_l\) gives \(E_P(Y-\widehat m_j\mid J=l,X)=m_l-\widehat m_j\).  Expanding \(\widehat U_j\), conditioning first on \((J,X)\), and summing over \(J\) yields the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P(\widehat U_j\mid X)-m_j
={}&(\widehat m_j-m_j)
 \left[1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}
 (1+\delta^A_{jj})(1+\delta^Z_{jj})\right]\\
&+\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\sum_{l\ne j}\pi_l
 \delta^A_{jl}\delta^Z_{jl}(m_l-\widehat m_j).
\end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, when \(l=j\) the two conditional bridge means are \(1+\delta^A_{jj}\) and \(1+\delta^Z_{jj}\); when \(l\ne j\), both indicator terms vanish and only the product of the two errors remains.

Latent positivity and the fitted half-margin give \(\pi_j^{-1}\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}\).  The true and fitted regressions are bounded by \(L\), because both laws use the declared bounded common outcome support.  Also
\[
 \left|1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}\right|
 \leq2\varepsilon^{-1}|\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|.
\]
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz over \(P_X\) to the first line of (11), and use (10); its integrated absolute value is at most
\[
 C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_m(r_\pi+r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c}).
\]
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to the product in the second line of (11), using fixed \(K\) and (10); its integrated absolute value is at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\).  Since \(E_Pm_j(X)=\psi_j\), the finite-dimensional norm satisfies
\[
 \|E_P\widehat U-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{r_m(r_\pi+r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\}. \tag{12}
\]
The mean of the fitted efficient score decomposes as
\[
 E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi
 =(E_P\widehat U-\psi)-E_P\widehat k.
\]
Combining (8), (12), and the corrected definition of \(\Delta_n\) proves the displayed bias bound.

For the derivative assertions, let \(t\mapsto\eta_t\) be a support-preserving two-sided regular factor path through the truth and evaluate its score mean under \(P=P_{\eta_0}\).  If only \(M_A\) varies, then \(m_t=m\), \(\pi_t=\pi\), and \(\delta^Z_t=0\), so (11) gives \(E_PU(\eta_t)-\psi=0\) for all sufficiently small \(t\).  Support preservation makes the exact conditional-zero cancellation applicable, and the preceding argument with \(r_Z=0\) gives
\[
 \|E_PQ(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A(t)
 \|Q(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)-QU\|_2=O(t^2),
\]
because DQM differentiability gives \(r_A(t)=O(|t|)\), while the separated inverse and Gram-gap bounds give an \(O(|t|)\) score displacement.  Hence the derivative of the mean bias at zero vanishes.

If only \(f\) varies coherently, then \(M_A,M_Z,\pi\), and \(B\) do not vary, so \(\delta^A_t=\delta^Z_t=0\) and (11) again gives \(E_PU(\eta_t)=\psi\).  The projector algebra gives \(B^{\mathsf T}N_t=0\); since every column of \(h_t=N_tc_t\) is also in \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\),
\[
 B^{\mathsf T}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}=0.
\]
Conditional three-view independence then gives, for every \(j\),
\[
 E_P\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\mid Y,J=j,X\}
 =\sum_{a,z}B_{(a,z),j}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}_{az}(Y,X)=0.
\]
Iterated expectation implies \(E_PQ_tU(\eta_t)=0\) exactly.  Thus the mean bias is identically zero along the coherent \(f\)-only path, proving the second derivative assertion.

Because \(D\mathbf 1_{K^2}=Bw\), the projector algebra gives \(N\mathbf 1_{K^2}=0\).  Therefore \(Qv=0\) for every nonrandom vector \(v\in\mathbb R^K\), coordinatewise: both \(Nv\) and its Gram right-hand side vanish.  The canonical-gradient definition consequently gives \(U-QU=\psi+\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\).  Set
\[
 S(O)=U(O)-QU(O)=\psi+\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O),
 \qquad \widehat S_f=\widehat U_f-\widehat Q_f\widehat U_f
\]
for training fold \(f\), and let \(n_f\) be its held-out size.  Adding and subtracting foldwise conditional means gives the exact decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)
={}&n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)\\
&+n^{-1/2}\sum_{f=1}^{F_{\mathrm{fold}}}
 \sum_{i:\,\mathrm{fold}(i)=f}
 \bigl[(\widehat S_f-S)(O_i)-P(\widehat S_f-S)\bigr]\\
&+n^{-1/2}\sum_{f=1}^{F_{\mathrm{fold}}}n_fP(\widehat S_f-\psi). \tag{13}
\end{aligned}
\]
Conditional on the training observations for fold \(f\), its held-out summands are independent and centered by the iid assumption, and the conditional second moment of the normalized fold sum is bounded by
\[
 \frac{n_f}{n}\|\widehat S_f-S\|_2^2. \tag{14}
\]
The established score-stability lemma and \(R_\Sigma=o_P(1)\) make (14) converge to zero in probability.  Conditional Markov inequality and the fixed number of folds therefore make the middle line of (13) \(o_P(1)\).

The condition \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\) invokes the support-cleaned quadratic-bias lemma on an event whose probability tends to one.  Consequently the last line of (13) is bounded in norm by
\[
 n^{-1/2}\sum_fn_f C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_{n,f}
 \leq\sqrt n\,C_{\mathrm{reg}}\max_f\Delta_{n,f}=o_P(1), \tag{15}
\]
where the last equality uses the fixed number of folds and the stated foldwise product-rate condition.  Thus
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_P(1). \tag{16}
\]
The threshold requirement \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\) makes the cleaning contribution compatible with \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\); the expansion itself uses the latter explicit condition.

The regularity margins, bounded outcome, fixed \(K\), and the Gram cutoff bound \(\|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2/\varepsilon\) bound both the true and fitted scores uniformly by a constant depending only on the regular stratum.  In particular \(E_P\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}=0\) and its covariance is \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  For fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^K\), the scalar Taylor formula for the complex exponential, with its uniformly bounded third-order remainder, gives
\[
 E_P\exp\{i t^{\mathsf T}\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}V_{\mathrm{eff}}t}{2n}+o(n^{-1}). \tag{17}
\]
Independence raises (17) to the \(n\)-th power, whose limit is \(\exp\{-t^{\mathsf T}V_{\mathrm{eff}}t/2\}\).  Applying this calculation to every fixed \(t\), and then (16), proves the asserted joint Gaussian limit.

For covariance consistency, score stability gives \(\widehat S_f\to S\) in \(L^2(P)\) on each fold.  Conditional on its training sample, independence and uniform boundedness give by a direct variance calculation
\[
 \left\|P_{n,f}(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})
 -P(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})\right\|_{\mathrm F}=o_P(1). \tag{18}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and \(L^2\) convergence give
\[
 \|P(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})-P(SS^{\mathsf T})\|_{\mathrm F}
 \leq\|\widehat S_f-S\|_2(\|\widehat S_f\|_2+\|S\|_2)=o_P(1). \tag{19}
\]
Summing over the fixed folds and using (16), hence \(\widehat\psi\to_P\psi\), shows that the empirical covariance centered at \(\widehat\psi\) converges to
\[
 E_P\{(S-\psi)(S-\psi)^{\mathsf T}\}
 =E_P(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\phi^{\mathrm{eff},\mathsf T})
 =V_{\mathrm{eff}}.
\]
This proves all conclusions.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(p,\widehat p\in[0,1]^K\) satisfy \(\sum_i p_i=\sum_i\widehat p_i=1\), let \(0<\tau<1/(2K)\), and define \(\bar p_i=\widehat p_i\mathbf 1\{\widehat p_i>\tau\}/\sum_l\widehat p_l\mathbf 1\{\widehat p_l>\tau\}\).  If \(\delta=\|\widehat p-p\|_\infty\), then the denominator is positive and
\[
 \|\bar p-p\|_\infty\leq(2K+1)(\delta+\tau).
\]
Moreover, if \(p_i=0\) and \(\delta\leq\tau\), then \(\bar p_i=0\).  Consequently, for the columnwise cleaning of \(\widehat M_A,\widehat M_Z\), on
\[
 \mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}
 =\{r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}\leq\tau_{S,n}\},
\]
every true-zero measurement cell is zero in \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\),
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{A,\infty}+\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{Z,\infty}+\tau_{S,n}),
\]
and the corresponding conditional \(L^2(P)\) errors are bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^{\mathrm c}\) and \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\).  No lower bound on a positive coordinate of \(p\), \(M_A\), or \(M_Z\) is required.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(t=\sum_{l:\,\widehat p_l\leq\tau}\widehat p_l\).  Because \(\widehat p\) is stochastic, \(0\leq t\leq K\tau<1/2\), and the normalizing denominator is \(1-t>0\).  If \(\widehat p_i>\tau\), then
\[
 |\bar p_i-\widehat p_i|
 =\widehat p_i\frac{t}{1-t}\leq\frac{K\tau}{1-K\tau}
 \leq2K\tau.
\]
If \(\widehat p_i\leq\tau\), then \(|\bar p_i-\widehat p_i|=\widehat p_i\leq\tau\).  The triangle inequality therefore gives
\[
 \|\bar p-p\|_\infty
 \leq\|\bar p-\widehat p\|_\infty+\|\widehat p-p\|_\infty
 \leq2K\tau+\delta
 \leq(2K+1)(\delta+\tau).
\]
If \(p_i=0\) and \(\delta\leq\tau\), then \(\widehat p_i\leq\tau\), so the strict threshold makes \(\bar p_i=0\).  Apply these conclusions to every column.  On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\), each of the two matrix sup-norm errors is at most \(\tau_{S,n}\), and hence every true-zero entry is removed.  The displayed matrix sup-norm bounds follow from equivalence of entrywise and operator norms in the fixed dimension \(K\).  Finally,
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_{L^2(P_X)}
 \leq \|\widehat M_A-M_A\|_{L^2(P_X)}
      +\|\bar M_A-\widehat M_A\|_{L^2(P_X)}
 \leq r_A+2K\tau_{S,n}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^{\mathrm c},
\]
and the same calculation applies to \(Z\).  The argument removes any fitted coordinate below the threshold and nowhere invokes a positive-cell lower bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), set \(a=\beta/(2\beta+d_X+1)\), and choose any fixed \(\gamma\) satisfying \(1/4<\gamma<a\), with \(\tau_{S,n}=n^{-\gamma}\).  If
\[
 r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=O_P(\rho_n),
 \qquad
 R_{\Sigma}-r_A^{\mathrm c}-r_Z^{\mathrm c}
 =O_P(\rho_n+\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad r_A+r_Z=O_P(\rho_n),
\]
then
\[
 r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad \tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4}),
 \qquad R_{\Sigma}=O_P(\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad \Delta_n=O_P(\tau_{S,n}^2)=o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Thus the support-cleaning requirements are compatible with the declared smoothness regime, although this implication does not assert that the named spline likelihood attains its antecedent rates.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The inequality \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\) is equivalent to
\[
 a=\frac{\beta}{2\beta+d_X+1}>\frac14.
\]
Hence a fixed \(\gamma\in(1/4,a)\) exists.  Because \(\rho_n=n^{-a}\) and \(\tau_{S,n}=n^{-\gamma}\),
\[
 \frac{\rho_n}{\tau_{S,n}}=n^{-(a-\gamma)}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 n^{1/4}\tau_{S,n}=n^{-(\gamma-1/4)}\longrightarrow0. \tag{20}
\]
The first antecedent and (20) give \((r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty})/\tau_{S,n}=o_P(1)\), while the second identity in (20) gives \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\).  By definition,
\[
 r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c}=r_A+r_Z+2\tau_{S,n}=O_P(\tau_{S,n}),
\]
because \(r_A+r_Z=O_P(\rho_n)=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\).  The remaining antecedent then yields \(R_\Sigma=O_P(\tau_{S,n})\).  Every factor in each product defining \(\Delta_n\) is \(O_P(\tau_{S,n})\), so
\[
 \Delta_n=O_P(\tau_{S,n}^2).
\]
Finally, \(n^{1/2}\tau_{S,n}^2=(n^{1/4}\tau_{S,n})^2\to0\) by (20).  This proves the result and also shows explicitly that it is a rate-propagation statement conditional on, not a proof of, the spline-likelihood antecedents.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For a foldwise support-cleaned coherent fit, put \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\), coordinatewise.  If \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), then \(P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n})\to1\).  On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\), every true-zero measurement cell is zero in \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\), the bounds
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{A,\infty}+\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{Z,\infty}+\tau_{S,n})
\]
hold without a beta-min condition on positive cells, and
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\right].
\]
Thus the support-cleaned correction has no first-order structural-zero leakage term.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old claim quantified additive leakage from an uncleaned fit. The corrected estimator thresholds and renormalizes first, so the valid claim is the exact-support and conditional-zero bound for the cleaned matrices on the screening event.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every support-cleaned coherent foldwise fit using \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\), the corrected \(\widehat N\), and the data-driven spectral inverse, if \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\), then, on an event whose probability tends to one,
\[
 \|E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n,
\]
where
\[
 \Delta_n=r_m(r_\pi+r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}
 +(r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})R_{\Sigma}.
\]
In particular, the pathwise derivative of the mean bias is zero along a support-preserving two-sided perturbation of \(M_A\) alone and along a coherent perturbation of \(f\) alone.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: After support cleaning, the former first-order leakage allowance is absent. The bridge and projection errors are controlled by the cleaned rates \(r_A^{\mathrm c}\) and \(r_Z^{\mathrm c}\), and the screening ratio must be imposed explicitly.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let every training-fold operator be formed from the support-cleaned matrices and use
\[
 \widehat N=I_{K^{2}}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B
 (\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B)^{+}\widehat B^{\mathsf T}.
\]
If, on every fold, \(R_{\Sigma}=o_P(1)\), \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\),
\[
 r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad \tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4}),
\]
then
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)\rightsquigarrow N(0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}),
\]
and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{eff}}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The inference theorem must explicitly require the support-screening and threshold window used by the corrected quadratic-bias lemma; \(R_{\Sigma}\) no longer contains the dimensionless screening ratio.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: On \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\) with \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), can the support-cleaned handle \(\mathfrak F\), using tensor-product B-splines of total dimension \(s_n\asymp n^{(d_X+1)/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\), be equipped with an explicit spline boundary or extension convention, a constrained likelihood parameterization, and a local likelihood-curvature inequality that jointly prove all of the following: the raw primitive \(L^2(P)\) rates for \((\widehat\pi,\widehat M_A,\widehat M_Z,\widehat f)\); essential-supremum rates strong enough that \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\) for some \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\); consistency of the empirical minimum-modal-gap permutation rule; and feasibility with probability tending to one of every cleaned-law half-margin restriction?  The support-cleaning rate-window lemma gives the admissible threshold window and the ensuing \(R_\Sigma\) and \(\Delta_n\) rates once the fitted likelihood and its cleaned plug-in coordinates satisfy that lemma's antecedents; no assertion that the listed \(L^2(P)\) coordinates alone imply \(R_\Sigma=O_P(\rho_n)\) or \(\Delta_n=O_P(\rho_n^2)\) is made.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: H\"older membership alone does not prove the named global spline-likelihood rate, uniform modal-label selection, or half-margin feasibility. The corrected question isolates those primitive, sup-norm, curvature, spline, and feasibility facts and removes the unsupported assertion that the \(L^2(P)\) coordinates alone deliver the old \(\rho_n^2\) remainder.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For each training fold, obtain one raw label-aligned product-factor fit \((\widehat m,\widehat\pi,\widehat M_A,\widehat M_Z,\widehat f)\) on the declared outcome support \(\mathcal Y\).  Choose \(\tau_{S,n}\) from the fold size and training data alone and apply the support-cleaning map to obtain \((\bar M_A,\bar M_Z)\).  The coherent fitted nuisance tuple uses \((\bar M_A,\bar M_Z)\), not the raw measurement matrices.  Retain only fitted laws satisfying the computable cleaned-law half-margin restrictions
\[
 \min_j\widehat\pi_j\geq\varepsilon/2,\qquad
 \min_{a,z}\widehat d_{az}\geq\varepsilon/2,
 \qquad \sigma_{\min}(\bar M_A)\wedge\sigma_{\min}(\bar M_Z)\geq\varepsilon/2,
\]
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat R^{\mathsf T}\widehat D\widehat R)\geq\varepsilon/2,
 \qquad
 \bar M_{A,jj}-\max_{a\ne j}\bar M_{A,aj}\geq\varepsilon/2
 \quad(j=1,\ldots,K).
\]
Set \(\widehat W=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat w)\), \(\widehat B=\bar M_A\odot\bar M_Z\), \(\widehat d=\widehat B\widehat w\), \(\widehat D=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat d)\), and \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\), and then set
\[
 \widehat N=I_{K^2}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B
 (\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B)^+
 \widehat B^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad \widehat h=\widehat N\widehat c.
\]
Form \(\widehat G\), \(\widehat b_{(\cdot)}\), and \(\widehat b_U\) as implications of this same cleaned product law.  With the known cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), define
\[
 \widehat Qf_0=\widehat Nf_0-
 \widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\widehat b_{f_0}.
\]
Neither a true measurement support, the true \(G\), nor \(\operatorname{rank}(G)\) is an input.

proposed.name: Support-cleaned coherent cross-fitted nuisance system
proposed.construction:
For each training fold, obtain one raw label-aligned product-factor fit \((\widehat m,\widehat\pi,\widehat M_A,\widehat M_Z,\widehat f)\) on the declared outcome support \(\mathcal Y\).  Choose \(\tau_{S,n}\) from the fold size and training data alone and apply the support-cleaning map to obtain \((\bar M_A,\bar M_Z)\).  The coherent fitted nuisance tuple uses \((\bar M_A,\bar M_Z)\), not the raw measurement matrices.  Retain only fitted laws satisfying the computable cleaned-law half-margin restrictions
\[
 \min_j\widehat\pi_j\geq\varepsilon/2,\qquad
 \min_{a,z}\widehat d_{az}\geq\varepsilon/2,
 \qquad \sigma_{\min}(\bar M_A)\wedge\sigma_{\min}(\bar M_Z)\geq\varepsilon/2,
\]
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat R^{\mathsf T}\widehat D\widehat R)\geq\varepsilon/2,
 \qquad
 \bar M_{A,jj}-\max_{a\ne j}\bar M_{A,aj}\geq\varepsilon/2
 \quad(j=1,\ldots,K).
\]
Set \(\widehat W=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat w)\), \(\widehat B=\bar M_A\odot\bar M_Z\), \(\widehat d=\widehat B\widehat w\), \(\widehat D=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat d)\), and \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\), and then set
\[
 \widehat N=I_{K^2}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B
 (\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B)^+
 \widehat B^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad \widehat h=\widehat N\widehat c.
\]
Form \(\widehat G\), \(\widehat b_{(\cdot)}\), and \(\widehat b_U\) as implications of this same cleaned product law.  With the known cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), define
\[
 \widehat Qf_0=\widehat Nf_0-
 \widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\widehat b_{f_0}.
\]
Neither a true measurement support, the true \(G\), nor \(\operatorname{rank}(G)\) is an input.

proposed.statement:
For a foldwise support-cleaned coherent fit, put \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\), coordinatewise.  If \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), then \(P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n})\to1\).  On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\), every true-zero measurement cell is zero in \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\), the bounds
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{A,\infty}+\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{Z,\infty}+\tau_{S,n})
\]
hold without a beta-min condition on positive cells, and
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\right].
\]
Thus the support-cleaned correction has no first-order structural-zero leakage term.

proposed.statement:
For every support-cleaned coherent foldwise fit using \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\), the corrected \(\widehat N\), and the data-driven spectral inverse, if \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\), then, on an event whose probability tends to one,
\[
 \|E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n,
\]
where
\[
 \Delta_n=r_m(r_\pi+r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}
 +(r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})R_{\Sigma}.
\]
In particular, the pathwise derivative of the mean bias is zero along a support-preserving two-sided perturbation of \(M_A\) alone and along a coherent perturbation of \(f\) alone.

open_obligations.partial_result: The deterministic part is closed.  Thresholding and renormalization use no true support, remove every true-zero cell with probability tending to one under \((r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty})/\tau_{S,n}=o_P(1)\), and perturb each measurement matrix by at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{\infty}+\tau_{S,n})\), without a beta-min condition. prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), the exact continuous-outcome canonical gradient is the product-bridge score minus a pointwise \(K^2\)-cell projection and one conditional Gram correction. Tangent-space completeness is supplied by the proved bounded differential lift. The implementable score now starts from one raw product fit, thresholds and renormalizes both measurement matrices without using their true supports, and recomputes every bridge and operator from that cleaned law. If the raw sup-norm error is \(o_P(\tau_{S,n})\), every true-zero cell is removed with probability tending to one and the bias is quadratic in the cleaned rates \(r_A+\tau_{S,n}\) and \(r_Z+\tau_{S,n}\). Efficient cross-fitted Gaussian and maximum-\(t\) inference follows under the displayed product and threshold rates.

project_justification.fill: The bounded differential-score lift closes tangent-space completeness and supports the exact finite canonical projector. For implementation, the paper uses one non-oracle product fit, a known analysis-class Gram cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), and a data-driven support-cleaning threshold. Thresholding and column renormalization remove true structural-zero measurement cells on a high-probability sup-norm screening event without assuming beta-min for positive cells; all posterior, bridge, and projector objects are recomputed from the cleaned law. The resulting remainder is quadratic in cleaned measurement errors. Proving that the specifically named global spline likelihood attains the needed primitive and uniform rates, modal-label stability, and cleaned half-margin feasibility remains an explicit open construction question.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each training fold first fits one raw label-aligned product law without using unknown measurement supports, the true conditional Gram matrix, or its rank. It then thresholds and renormalizes both measurement matrices at the data-chosen \(\tau_{S,n}\), and recomputes every bridge, posterior, projection, and score object from that cleaned law. The Gram inverse retains fitted eigenvalues above the known analysis-class cutoff \(\varepsilon/2\).

prose_updates.related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) are the closest theorem-level comparator: their Theorems 2--4 treat the binary observed tangent space and influence functions, and Supplement S8.2 obtains the continuous-outcome efficiency bound through a refining outcome partition. The present multilevel construction instead uses the exact \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) and one conditional Gram solve. Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026) supply the categorical inverse-feature product-bridge precursor, but not observed-data canonicality or the support-cleaned projected-score remainder. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009), Hu and Schennach (2008), and Deaner (2023) inform latent-factor identification; none supplies the measurable bounded differential inverse proved here. Tsiatis and Ma (2004) inform nuisance-score projection, Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016) inform coherent repeated-measurement estimation, and Tsybakov (2009) informs the smooth sieve benchmark. None of those cited results establishes the specific spline-likelihood curvature, uniform modal-label selection, and cleaned half-margin feasibility left open here. The implementation uses neither a true measurement support nor a true Gram rank; design-known supports remain only an optional specialization.
prose_updates.interpretation: The efficiency conclusion rests on equality with the full observed-data DQM tangent closure, not projection onto a convenient latent submodel. Non-oracle implementation has two separate stability devices. The known separated-model margin permits the spectral cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\). Unknown measurement supports are handled constructively: fitted probabilities at or below \(\tau_{S,n}\) are set to zero, each column is renormalized, and every downstream score object is rebuilt. On \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}\leq\tau_{S,n}\), all true zeros are exactly restored, while positive cells may also be removed without invalidating the bound because the total perturbation is only \(O(r_\infty+\tau_{S,n})\). Thus no beta-min condition is hidden. The price is a cleaned first-stage rate of order \(r+\tau_{S,n}\), not the raw \(r\) alone.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The results apply to the declared quantitatively separated, two-sided pathwise-interior specialization, not to the full published Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen or Bian--Zhou--Cui classes. The bounded differential inverse uses the posterior and projection-Gram gaps, and the Gram selector uses the known analysis-class margin \(\varepsilon\). Support cleaning requires \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\); efficient inference additionally uses \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\) and the explicit cleaned product remainder. H\"older membership by itself does not prove the global spline-likelihood curvature, sup-norm rates, uniform modal-label selection, or high-probability feasibility of all fitted half-margins.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Exact identification, tangent completeness, the finite projector, canonicality, strict variance reduction, the binary comparison, and the continuous witness hold on the declared fixed-\(K\), quantitatively separated, two-sided pathwise-interior model. Cross-fitted implementation uses neither unknown true measurement supports nor an oracle Gram rank: it support-cleans a raw product fit and selects Gram directions at the known cutoff \(\varepsilon/2\). Its inference theorem is conditional on the raw sup-norm screening rate, \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\), and the displayed cleaned product rates. Establishing those rates and fitted feasibility for the named B-spline product likelihood is still open. Modal ties, local singularity, failure of common outcome support, and failure of the screening window remain outside delivery. The maternal-smoking application is prospective because the published six-bin study does not itself verify paired-proxy conditional independence or the quantitative separation conditions.
